comparator.name: Bachelor Creative Technology - Amsterdam (VU-UT)
comparator.institution: University of Twente / Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 Creative Technology regulations confirm eight 15 EC modules, 30 EC of elective space and a 30 EC graduation semester. The example uses the Humane by Design specialisation and its Dangerous Design unit in module eight. The graduation project is completed in two parts worth 5 and 15 EC, alongside Academic Writing and Reflection.

alternatives.label: Creative computing, design & digital society
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines programming, data and AI with product design, user research, communication and the societal effects of technology.
alternatives.concept: Combine programming, machine learning and data analysis with product prototyping, creative communication and user research. Study how people and organisations use digital products and how choices about fairness and accountability shape their development.

alternatives.label: AI, data & smart systems
alternatives.labelReason: Four mathematics and systems courses replace four design, qualitative and organisational courses, making intelligent data-driven systems the differentiating strand.
alternatives.concept: Use programming, algorithms and machine learning to analyse data and model smart systems. Study signals and probability, and apply mathematics to robot motion and planning. Ethics and market research add perspectives on how such systems are used.
alternatives.distinctness: 5 courses (37.5 EC) differ each way from the closest option. This plan emphasises computation, signals and robotics.

alternatives.label: Human-centred interaction & technology

alternatives.distinctness: 7 courses (52.5 EC) differ each way from the closest option. This plan emphasises cognition, behaviour and qualitative user enquiry.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the Amsterdam location of the joint Creative Technology bachelor. The current VU curriculum identifies Humane by Design as the Amsterdam-delivered specialisation and lists it first, while all three choices remain open to students. It is therefore the most location-representative route for this exact target, selected independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad closest response is feasible. The official AI/data/smart-technology and human-centred interaction strands each support a coherent additional curriculum with material course consequences. All three pass qualitative and pairwise 30-EC distinctness, so production stops at the permitted maximum.

blocks: Introduction to Programming addresses the programming foundation inside this broad introductory module, without reproducing its full multidisciplinary scope.
Introduction to Data Science addresses data processing and visualisation, while the comparator module additionally physicalises data through an installation.
Machine Learning directly addresses the AI and machine-learning core, without the comparator's dedicated-hardware project.
Twente integrates programming, physical computing, circuits and visualisation in a smart-environment project.
Both frame problems around users and consider how ideas can become solutions. UCR focuses on entrepreneurship and value propositions.
Consumer Product Design directly develops user-needs analysis, prototyping and iterative evaluation, while the comparator focuses specifically on human-computer interaction.
Both examine the social effects of technical choices. UCR’s AI Ethics covers fairness, bias and accountability, while Humane by Design also develops future scenarios and design projects.
Both develop written argument and communication. The Amsterdam course applies academic writing to the graduation project.
Both explore how creative choices shape an audience’s experience. UCR works through language, sound and performance, while Twente develops interactive installations.
Twente reserves 30 EC for approved electives, a minor or exchange.
Twente requires an individual design and research project. UCR offers independent research separately.
The graduation semester includes a dedicated reflection unit tied to the design project.

notes.text: UCR offers related study in computing, product prototyping, cognition and communication. Twente integrates electronics, physical computing and interactive installations through a sequence of studio and laboratory projects.

audience.programmeDescription: The joint University of Twente and VU Amsterdam Creative Technology degree combines computing, electronics, human-centred design and interactive media. The Amsterdam example includes Humane by Design, with work on future scenarios and fairness in data science.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The three UCR options explore creative computing and product design, AI and smart systems, or human interaction with technology. The Amsterdam curriculum combines its fairness and design work with physical computing, interactive installations and an individual graduation project.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC example includes 30 EC of approved elective study and a 30 EC graduation semester.

componentNotes.m5-humane-design: Includes Fairness in Data Science and a project on designing futures. Module eight includes Dangerous Design.
componentNotes.y3-electives: Entry normally requires all 60 EC from year one and at least 30 EC from year two.
componentNotes.y3-project: Normally follows completion of modules 1–8. The 5 EC first part must be completed before the 15 EC second part.
